subject: Re: SageTech — long-run price safeguard request
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sagetech.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@sagetech.com
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-year protection request — SageTech/Redwood

Hi Jonas and Vanessa,

Thanks again for the product demo today. We’re pretty far along internally and procurement asked me to surface one last ask before we move to legal: SageTech is planning a 3-year commitment to Redwood capacity, but they need a contractual assurance that per-unit pricing will not increase above a fixed cap during the committed period and that any renewal will not reprice the committed baseline upward without notice and a right to opt-out.

Specifically: 3-year term, initial per-token price locked for 24 months, then a maximum uplift of 5% year-over-year thereafter; automatic renewal protections that prevent mid-term repricing on committed units; and an explicit clause that caps annual uplift at 5% even at renewal for the first renewal term.

We recognize this is non-standard. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a variant like this and what approvals or concessions (discounting, SLA commits, or minimums) would be required? Procurement expects a short MAAP before legal.

Attached: their internal forecast (see procurement).

Best,
Elena
Director, Strategic Sourcing
SageTech

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sagetech.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year protection request — SageTech/Redwood

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the forecast. I looped in Vanessa (deal desk) to scope out approvals and Markus (finance) to model the long-run impact. We can put together a MAAP and a proposed legal clause, but the request touches two levers that require executive sign-off: (1) a price lock beyond 12 months, and (2) an uplift cap that constrains future pricing flexibility.

Quick internal ask to SageTech: can you confirm committed QPS and a target monthly spend floor? That will materially affect the offer.

I’ll follow up internally and get back with a proposed trade (discount vs. uplift cap) by end of day.

— Jonas
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SageTech pricing ask — need exec approval

Team — forwarding Elena’s note and my read. Summary of trade we can offer without making the company materially inflexible:

- Term: 3 years committed capacity (reserved pool).
- Price lock: lock on published per-token price for first 18 months.
- Uplift cap: 5% max annual uplift starting month 19, measured on the base per-token rate.
- Renewal protection: for the committed baseline, first renewal term also capped at 5% for the portion of committed units; any overage units move to list pricing.
- Concession required for Redwood: 12% one-time up-front commitment discount spread over year-1 invoices (effectively ~10% NPV depending on payment cadence), plus a 99.95% P99 latency SLA and 24x7 support for the duration.

I ran a quick back-of-envelope with Markus but the attached is the clean sheet. The material risk to Redwood is if model costs or GPU supply change materially — that’s why finance needs visibility and exec buy-in.

Asks for exec approval:
1) Approve the 18-month hard price lock + 5% uplift cap thereafter for SageTech with the proposed 12% up-front commitment discount.
2) Authorize the SLA bump (99.95% P99) tied to a 10% fee credit if we miss monthly SLOs (caps in contract).
3) Approve deal desk to sign MAAP and send draft to SageTech legal; execs will sign final contract.

Attachments: pricing-breakdown-3yr.pdf, SageTech-MAAP-v3.ods

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SageTech pricing ask — need exec approval

Thanks Vanessa — read and modeled. Short take: I support offering the structure with the following guardrails to protect Redwood economics and optionality:

1) Make the 18-month price lock unconditional only if SageTech posts a 9-month prepaid commitment (or equivalent escrow). Otherwise limit unconditional lock to 12 months and provide the 6-month extension only after they hit committed utilization targets in months 3–6.
2) Keep the uplift cap at 5% but tie it to an index clause: uplift capped at the higher of 5% or CPI + 2% (rounded), not to exceed 7% (this preserves some cost alignment).
3) Add a force-majeure manufacturing/hardware-cost pass-through narrowly scoped to wholesale GPU price changes that are certified by our procurement team and limited to a single annual pass-through event.
4) Approve SLA bump and credit cap (max exposure 1.5% of annual contract value).

If we get exec sign-off on these guardrails I’ll work with legal to craft the clause language. Approve in principle?

— Lauren
VP, Commercial Operations

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SageTech pricing ask — need exec approval

Quick note from finance and exec: I approve the offer with Lauren’s guardrails. Net impact using our 3-year demand scenarios: worst case (low utilization) reduces gross margin by ~4.2% in year 1 but recovers to ~1.1% by year 3 as committed spend floors kick in. The prepaid option materially reduces risk (improves NPV by ~7%).

Markus (on behalf of exec committee)
CFO, Redwood Inference
